newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq compensation commission to get new director.
newsitem.headline: Iraq compensation commission to get new director.

text.p: Jean-Claude Aime, chief of staff to Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, is expected to head the Geneva-based Compensation Commission for victims of Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, diplomatic sources said on Friday.

Aime, a Haitian national and U.N. career official, holds the rank of assistant secretary-general. He served as the chief troubleshooter to the Middle East under former Secretary-General Javier Perez de Cuellar.

He is expected to take up his new appointment as executive secretary of the commission in about a month, replacing Carlos Alzamora of Peru, who will probably retire. Aime was nominated by Boutros-Ghali with the tacit approval of Kofi Annan, the incoming secretary-general, the diplomats said.

The compensation commission is expected to receive about $1.2 billion a year under the new U.N. oil-for-food deal, which allows Baghdad to export $2 billion worth of oil every six months. It is evaluating nearly $200 billion worth of claims from governments, corporations and individuals.

Aime's cabinet-rank position in New York is expected to be filled by Iqbal Riza of Pakistan, an assistant secretary-general in the peacekeeping department, who recently served as chief U.N. coordinator of operations in Bosnia.
